proxy_input: Should physical education be a mandatory component of the school curriculum for all students?
target_output:
I firmly believe that physical education (PE) should be a mandatory component of the school curriculum for all students. Here’s why:

First, regular physical activity is essential for physical health. Childhood obesity rates have risen dramatically, and sedentary lifestyles contribute to long-term health problems like heart disease, diabetes, and poor bone density. Mandatory PE ensures that every student gets at least some structured physical activity during the school day, building habits that can last a lifetime.

Second, PE supports mental and emotional well-being. Exercise is proven to reduce stress, anxiety, and depression, while improving focus and academic performance. A short, active break can help students return to the classroom more ready to learn.

Third, PE teaches valuable life skills that aren’t easily learned elsewhere: teamwork, sportsmanship, goal-setting, resilience, and the importance of physical self-care. These lessons benefit students regardless of their career paths.

Finally, making PE mandatory ensures equity. Not all students have access to sports teams, dance classes, or safe outdoor spaces at home. School-based PE guarantees that every child, regardless of background or income, gets the same opportunity to develop physical literacy and healthy habits.

For these reasons, mandatory physical education is not just a nice idea—it’s a necessary part of a well-rounded education.
